findings.claim: The signed reviewed commit contains the four registrar artifacts. Every artifact binding carried by the execution bundle resolves to the recorded SHA-256, and the execution bundle has zero errors against its frozen JSON Schema.
findings.limitation: No dedicated frozen schema was found for the event log, boundary receipt or semantic stop receipt; those artifacts were checked for binding and internal consistency, not schema conformance.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the registrar artifacts and signed commit unchanged.

findings.claim: The artifacts contain 208 ordered unique query events, 1034 raw result records, 609 unique canonical URLs, and exactly matching 609-entry candidate and exposure projections. All exposure entries are requested false. The proposed allowlist contains 329 HTML entries.
findings.limitation: Counts and zero-boundary assertions are derivable only from committed artifacts and receipts; this offline adviser did not observe provider calls and cannot independently prove events outside the recorded transcript.
findings.recommendation: Treat these as artifact-backed execution claims, not external network attestation.

findings.claim: The stopped bundle overlaps predecessor exposure. Independent canonical recomputation finds 10 overlaps in the immediate structural-preflight ledger and 23 overlaps across its complete bound predecessor chain. Every listed URL remains exposed and unavailable for unseen-edition evidence.
findings.limitation: The predecessor lineage itself states that earlier aggregate exposure reconstruction is incomplete, so 23 is a verified lower bound rather than proof of complete historical non-overlap.
findings.recommendation: Keep the execution terminal and failed. Carry all 609 successor exposures plus the complete cumulative predecessor lineage into any future denylist.

findings.claim: The successor verifier's _known_denied_urls function reads only the immediate ledger and does not traverse its bound predecessor. Its generic stop is correct because the immediate set already overlaps, but it undercounts cumulative overlap and cannot establish full lineage non-overlap.
findings.limitation: This does not invalidate the fail-closed outcome; it makes the recorded reason less complete than the cumulative evidence.
findings.recommendation: Prospectively fix the verifier to traverse the complete digest-bound predecessor chain with cycle and depth controls, then add tests proving inherited overlaps stop execution. Do not rewrite this stopped bundle.

findings.claim: The bundle, boundary receipt and 209-event registrar log consistently record zero result, landing-page, source-file, HEAD and redirect requests, zero persisted snippets, excerpts and target facts, and no candidate or source-content opening. Result objects contain titles and URLs but no snippet field.
findings.limitation: This is consistent digest-bound self-reporting, not an independently captured packet trace or provider-side audit log.
findings.recommendation: Retain the zero-request/no-snippet claim with this limitation and make no broader claim about provider internals.

findings.claim: Fail-closed stopping was required by the frozen non-overlap contract. The execution cannot proceed to selector or candidate acquisition and supplies no G2 passage evidence.
findings.limitation: A future owner decision may authorize a new prospectively frozen lineage, but cannot convert this failed execution into a pass.
findings.recommendation: Accept the stop as immutable failed evidence only.

options.description: Accept this execution as terminal failed evidence, fix cumulative-ledger traversal and tests, and prepare a separately identified candidate-frame redesign that excludes all known exposures before any new network activity.
options.trade_offs: Strongest evidence integrity and simplest lineage; requires new design and owner authorization and does not advance G2 immediately.
options.contingency: If a sufficiently large unexposed metadata frame cannot be frozen without adaptive searching, terminate the blind-holdout route and redesign the evidence question.

options.description: Retain the 609 records only as an exposed metadata discovery census, never as unseen holdout candidates, after prospectively fixing the verifier and creating a separate use contract.
options.trade_offs: Preserves bounded discovery value but cannot support the approved blind-holdout claim and adds governance complexity.
options.contingency: If separation between exposed discovery and unseen evaluation cannot be enforced mechanically, discard this option and use Option A.

options.description: Preserve the stop and take no additional repository action.
options.trade_offs: No further exposure or implementation risk, but G2 remains blocked and the verifier-depth defect remains open.
options.contingency: Return to Option A before any future successor design.

recommendation: Choose Option A. Preserve the execution and its registrar artifacts unchanged as terminal failed evidence; prospectively correct cumulative exposure traversal and negative tests; construct any future frame only after removing every known exposed URL, edition and series; and return a new digest-bound design to the sole owner before any network or source access.
rationale: The immediate-ledger overlap is sufficient to require the current stop, while the 23 cumulative overlaps and incompletely reconstructable earlier exposure make retrospective acceptance scientifically unsafe. A prospective correction preserves auditability without wasting the bounded search as lineage evidence.
conflicts: The bundle's non-overlap receipt records no known overlaps, but independent recomputation finds 10 immediate and 23 cumulative overlaps.
The successor verifier checks only the immediate exposure ledger even though that ledger explicitly binds a predecessor chain.
abstentions: No opinion is offered on the factual relevance, exact-edition identity, rights status or structural eligibility of any result.
No network call, result URL, landing page, file or source content was accessed during this review.
